To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) WSOL is ill posed, 2) existing methods are not significantly better than CAM, 3) WSOL has not reached the few-shot learning baseline, 4) the evaluation protocols are flawed and 5) the future directions of WSOL are to be discussed.
(i) existing WSOL methods are not competitive with few shot learning baseline and (ii) the WSOL task is not well posed with only image-level labels.
the current WSOL methods have failed to improve the state of the art and have not reached the baseline performance of few shot learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: “How well can we do WSOL with image level labels?”.
the question: “How good are the WSOL methods in practice?” and we find that the answer to this question is: “Not very good”.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WSOL task is not yet solved.
the field of WSOL has not yet reached a point where it can be used for practical applications.
the WSOL problem is not well posed, and the current methods are not able to solve it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the field has not yet achieved the full potential of WSOL.
WSOL task has not been well defined and the current evaluation protocol is not suitable to assess WSOL methods.
the WSOL task is not well posed and that we should be more careful in evaluating and comparing methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the recent progress, the WSOL task is still in an early stage and requires more attention to the evaluation protocol and the design of the methods.
, despite the promise of WSOL methods, there has been little progress in the field over the last five years.
WSOL task should be evaluated under a more stringent protocol to be able to assess its true performance.
